The E-1 license is the unlimited electrical contractor license, while the E-2 license is the unlimited electrical journeyperson license. pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Connecticut requires electricians to be licensed by the Department of Consumer Protection in order to perform electrical work. The Department of Consumer Protection licenses individuals, and the state recognizes both limited and unlimited license categories. Contractor licenses generally use odd numbers, such as E-1, while journeyperson or employee licenses generally use even numbers, such as E-2. The E-1 Unlimited Electrical Contractor license is the broad unlimited contractor-level electrical license in Connecticut. The holder of the E-1 license is permitted to perform all electrical work as defined under Connecticut electrical licensing rules. The E-2 Unlimited Electrical Journeyperson license also permits broad electrical work, but only while the license holder is employed by a properly licensed contractor. Only contractors can obtain permits and sign contracts in Connecticut. Journeypersons and apprentices cannot work directly for consumers unless employed by, or employing, a licensed contractor of record.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: A balanced preparation plan is important because the exam covers a wide range of electrical work and may include trade knowledge or general industry practices. Calculations should be practiced regularly. Candidates should work on identifying the correct formula, reading the question carefully, converting units properly, using the correct code table, and checking whether the answer is reasonable. The calculations guide helps candidates slow down and build repeatable habits instead of relying on guesswork during the exam. Code navigation should be part of nearly every study session. Candidates should practice using the table of contents, index, definitions, article layout, tables, notes, exceptions, and cross-references. Open-book testing rewards candidates who know where to look and how to confirm answers efficiently. Flash cards are useful for short study sessions and repetition. They help candidates reinforce important terms, calculations, safety topics, and code-related concepts when they do not have time for a full practice exam.
